ops.title: Eliminate repeated heartbeat cursor history rewrites
ops.description:
Runner.check previously serialized and published the complete RUNNER action history for each heartbeat cursor. The fix commits one cursor per contiguous heartbeat group, keeps lane leases immediate with original timestamps, and flushes before non-heartbeat effects and delivery acknowledgement.

Paired real Runner.check CI at 32/10000 historical actions and 32/100 heartbeats reproduces the old cost: 100 heartbeats with 10000 historical actions wrote 489807092 logical JSON bytes in 100 publications; the identical candidate fixture asserts one publication. Effect-boundary and crash-replay fixtures pass. PR1187 merged dace60d8; 0.7.644/public02347e0d is installed with exact byte hashes and naturally running in both Orca and landing controllers. Main CI3917pytest/1008pack passes. No physical IO attribution or savings claim.

Evidence: /Users/yasyf/.local/state/host-pressure-recovery/runs/20261026T235128-repeat/fundamental-efficiency/long-running-heartbeat-final-runtime-receipt.json; /Users/yasyf/.local/state/host-pressure-recovery/runs/20261026T235128-repeat/fundamental-efficiency/long-running-heartbeat-paired-ci.json; /Users/yasyf/.local/state/host-pressure-recovery/runs/20261026T235128-repeat/fundamental-efficiency/long-running-heartbeat-native-adoption.json. Broader SQLite/corpus work remains separate and open.

ops.text: Preserve immediate lease timestamps, cursor durability before external effects, and crash replay behavior.
Actual Runner.check paired CI proves one RUNNER cursor publication per contiguous heartbeat group independent of heartbeat count.
Merge, publish, install exact reviewed bytes, and verify natural Orca and landing controller adoption.
